legend: Classic spindle cell lipoma composed of bland spindle cells, mature adipocytes, ropy collagen bundles, and a fibromyxoid stroma.
Spindle cell lipoma (myxoid pattern) showing abundant myxoid stroma.
Spindle cell lipoma (pseudoangiomatous pattern) showing branching and dilated vascular-like spaces separating the spindle cells and stroma to form pseudopapillary projections.
Spindle cells are arranged in short fascicles with nuclear palisading.
Pleomorphic and multinucleated floret-like giant cells are seen in pleomorphic lipoma.
Note adipocytes, spindle cells, and ropy collagenous fibres.
source: Dr Jennifer Brown & Dr Zsolt Orosz, Department of Pathology, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford University Hospitals, UK

legend: Higher magnification of the lesion does not show atypia.

legend: Sagittal T1-weighted and fat-saturated proton density (PD) imaging in the midline of the neck. A heterogeneously high T1 signal, suppressed on the fat-saturated imaging, is indicative of intralesional fat content (shown here). The heterogeneous signal is suggestive of an atypical fat tumour, rather than a simple lipoma, with the location classic for spindle cell lipoma (Fig. <<#56713>>).
source: Dr Huw Walters and Dr Rajat Chowdhury, Department of Radiology, Nuffield Orthopaedic Centre, Oxford, UK
